Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

hit verb

a ball, with a bat, a racket or the hand

also hit the ball, strike the ball, return the ball, hit back, hit the ball out of the park, a hit (baseball)

classical

Traupman 45, 50
Andresian p. 20 (manū pulsāre)
Traupman 328

pulsō, pulsāre, pulsāvī, pulsātum

verb, first conjugation

To push, strike, beat (Cic.): Traupman’s verb for hitting a ball, as pede pulsāre is kicking it (see kick); with the hand, manū pulsāre.

Other words

  • percutiō, percutere, percussī, percussum

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Vīv. Exerc. 22

    To strike hard, to hit (Cic.); Vives’s verb for hitting the ball at tennis.

  • repercutiō, repercutere, repercussī, repercussum — hit back, make rebound

    verb, third conjugation · also used · post-classical · Andresian p. 20

    Post-Augustan, chiefly of light and sound thrown back (Ov., Verg., Tac.); Lewis & Short cites a discus that rebounds.

  • expulsō, expulsāre — hit back, keep hitting (a ball)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Mart. 14.46.1

    Martial’s ball speaks; Varro has pilā expulsim lūdere, play ball hitting it back and forth (Lewis & Short s.v. pila).

  • repellō, repellere, reppulī, repulsum — return (a ball)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · M-O s.v. ball: return (ball), hit back

    Morgan–Owens’s verb for returning a ball, after Mercuriale’s repulsus.

  • pulsus, pulsūs m. — a hit (in baseball)

    noun, fourth declension · also used · modern · Traupman 328

    Classically a push or blow, a beat (Lewis & Short); of a hit in baseball, Traupman.

Examples

  • sī mē nōbilibus scīs expulsāre sinistrīs, sum tua. tū nescīs? rūstice, redde pilam

    if you can hit me back with a fine left hand, I’m yours. You can’t? Give the ball back, bumpkin!Mart. 14.46.1–2

  • Quōmodo ergō percutiunt pilam? pugnō, ut follēs? — Nē sīc quidem, sed rēticulō.

    How do they hit the ball, then? With their fist, like footballs? — Not that either: with a racket.Vīv. Exerc. 22

  • pilam extrā campum lūsōrium pulsāre

    hit the ball out of the parkTraupman 45

See also ball, kick, racket, bat, throw, catch.
